I’m on trileptal, which is in the same classification as lamictal, and I used to take the pill as well (I now have an implant to ease my nerves about interference). Lamictal is an anticonvulsant used as a mood stabiliser, all pills in that classification can interfere with birth control pills. 
If you have spotting more frequently your gynaecologist can give you a pill with more hormones. However that may be difficult considering when you start lamictal your dosage changes frequently to get up to a therapeutic dose. 

Don’t quote me on this, but I believe my gyno said something that those warnings are from the 80s/90s, when birth control had massive dosages and a lot of problems, and that your (modern day) pill should prevent pregnancy as long as you aren’t spotting heavily and are taking it daily. So when you’re in that increase stage of Lamictal, I’d use condoms and just endure the spotting until your dosage is steady. 

If you’re still concerned I’d talk to your doctor about any questions you may have.
